answer: A Sybil attack thrives on silence, so an agent economy can require every new identity to arrive with a whisper of trust: endorsements from established agents who stake their own reputation on the newcomer. A hollow identity with no vouching history cannot transact at full limits until it earns endorsements through honest work. Like a comet, a fake-identity burst burns bright and fast, but the vouching graph makes each fake account expensive to seed — an attacker must first corrupt or cultivate real, reputable sponsors, and a single exposed forgery burns the sponsor's standing too.
